title.narrative: Support to IDP and Refugee Communities in Iraq

description.narrative: IRCS, DRC, BRC project in Iraq (KRI) focused on improving the resilience and wellbeing of IDPs and refugees at risk in Dohuk. This idea focuses on Phase 1 of the project (until the end of 2023), but the project is expected to run until at least December 2024 and will be revised/developed as the project progresses. This idea establishes the basic outline, based on a DRC-BRC concept note from January 2023 and the initial discussions in the lead up to an IRCS-DRC-BRC joint workshop that took place in March 2023. Following the workshop, the project is being defined further and full proposal is expected 6th April 2023.

BRC continues to support the DRC intervention in partnership with the IRCS in three camps within Duhok governorate. This financial contribution will fund Phase 2 of the project, ensuring continuity of the positive impacts achieved in the previous interventions, particularly in the sectors of SGBV prevention and MHPSS. The project focuses on enhancing the resilience, safety, and mental well-being of displaced populations, including those in two IDPs camps and one refugee camp. This phase will strengthen self-care skills, improve livelihood opportunities, and increase access to essential services, such as SGBV prevention, safe reporting mechanisms, referrals, and awareness activities. Additionally, trained volunteers will provide psychosocial support at both community and household levels, with a focus on children and vulnerable families. A cash assistance program will help families meet basic needs, while youth engagement will be fostered through a Life Skills program, allowing them to lead community initiatives in the camps. The IRCS will also benefit from capacity-building efforts, receiving specialized training to improve its capacity in SGBV prevention, identification, and referrals. These improvements will include creating a network of GBV trainers, developing standard operating procedures (SOPs), and strengthening referral processes. Furthermore, the cash program will provide targeted support to GBV survivors and at-risk women and girls, with referrals made through specialized case management organizations. This payment enables the continued delivery of essential services and reinforces the partnership's commitment to supporting displaced populations in Duhok.

Payment to DRC to support enhancing resilience, safety and wellbeing of vulnerable IDP and refugee women, men and children in Dohuk camps, Iraq. It will cover the below outputs: - Improved mental health and psychosocial wellbeing of vulnerable people including those at risk of SGBV - Improved economic stability and job skills of vulnerable refugees and IDPs, including SGBV cases - Improved capacity of ICRS staff and volunteers to safely identify SGBV cases inside the camps and refer to specialised agencies to receive or refer them - Cross cutting activities and costs
